newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures climb to sharp gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures climb to sharp gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures clipped their biggest gains during the final 30 minutes but still finished sharply higher.

March Standard & Poor's 500 futures backed off their new all-time high of 778.20 on long profit-taking and as shares of Intel Corp sliced their gains before the company's fourth quarter earnings news after Tuesday's close, brokers said.

"Intel started to come off...plus profit-taking," said one S&P 500 futures floor broker of reasons for the late erosion. "A lot of these guys were long all day," he said, adding that longs wanted to get flat before Intel earnings were announced.
Shares of Intel Corp ended up 1/4 at 147-1/8, off the day's peak at 149-3/4. After Tuesday's close, Intel reported earnings of $2.13 per share versus $0.98 and against First Call consensus of $1.84.

Earlier on Tuesday, March S&P 500s had ratcheted upward in fits and starts fueled by occasional buy stops hit as locals and dealers took turns buying, forcing out those who were probing for a top, brokers said.
"It just seems like one house after another does a little bit of buying," said a floor analyst. "It's very mixed activity. It gets really quiet and then they push them."
Traders said price boards showed estimated volume in March S&P 500 futures at a healthy 90,000 contracts Tuesday.
The stock market rally lifted the Dow 30 industrials index more than 50 points and near midday triggered the New York Stock Exchange's curb on computer-assisted programs trading.
But traders said before the curb took effect, futures held a rich premium over cash and attracted several rounds of arbitrage buy programs.
Futures had sprinted upward at the outset, hitting the five-point opening price limit, buoyed partly by a technically assisted rally in U.S. Treasury bond futures.

T-bond futures and equities got an added boost from data suggesting U.S. economic growth is controlled enough to keep inflation at bay, reducing the likelihood of a near-term U.S. rate hike, brokers said.
Debt futures gained early when December U.S. consumer prices rose 0.3 percent, as forecast, but the core rate firmed 0.1 percent, slightly below forecasts for up 0.2 percent.

March S&P 500s ended up 8.90 points at 773.20, Value Lines rose 4.45 to 701.60, Nikkei added 60.0 to 17,960.0, Midcap rose 2.60 to 264.75, NYSE Composite gained 4.05 to 407.25, Russell rose 3.60 to 371.85, NASDAQ jumped 18.75 to 891.00.
